newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ ends weaker, trade thin before USDA report.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ ends weaker, trade thin before USDA report.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled weaker amid expectations for an upward revision to Florida's output estimate, market sources said.

Many industry sources have anticipated a retreat from recent highs, citing a fundamental situation that includes ample supplies from both Florida and Brazil, and high retail prices that have kept a lid on demand.

Additional pressure could come Tuesday when the U.S. Department of Agriculture issues its supply and demand report. Analysts expect the USDA to raise its box count by 500,000 to 1.5 million boxes from its latest estimate for a record 220 million 90-lb boxes.
The USDA will release its estimate at 0830 EST.

"I think the industry is aware of it but I'm not sure how the specs will look at (an increase)," Dean Witter vice president Celeste Georgakis, said. "They've been looking for a cut and we simply don't feel at this point in time that much has changed."
Analysts said overpicking in the early and mids would be the reason for the increase in Tuesday's report.
May juice ended 1.95 weaker at 85.00 cents per pound, having ranged from 86.90 to 84.75 cents. March expired at 83.40 cents, down 1.35.
Volume was estimated at 2,500 lots compared with the official 2,655 lots on Friday.
Speculators and locals were cited on both sides of the market while the trade was noted as a scale-down buyer.
